definition: In image processing and computer vision, a scale space framework can be used to represent an image as a family of gradually smoothed images.
details: This framework is very general and a variety of scale space representations exist. A typical approach for choosing a particular type of scale space representation is to establish a set of scale-space axioms, describing basic properties of the desired scale-space representation and often chosen so as to make the representation useful in practical applications. Once established, the axioms narrow the possible scale-space representations to a smaller class, typically with only a few free parameters. A set of standard scale space axioms, discussed below, leads to the linear Gaussian scale-space, which is the most common type of scale space used in image processing and computer vision.

explainer.lead: Scale-space axioms are a set of basic properties chosen to define what a desired scale-space representation of an image should satisfy. They matter because fixing these axioms narrows the range of possible representations to a small class, typically with only a few free parameters.

tiers.eli5: Instead of trying every possible way to blur a picture at many levels, you first agree on a few ground rules, and that leaves only a handful of sensible options.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use the axioms to pick a principled scale-space representation rather than an arbitrary one. A pitfall is choosing axioms that suit theory but do not match the practical needs of the application.
tiers.paperLevel: A scale space represents an image as a family of gradually smoothed images; the axioms describe basic properties of the desired representation and narrow the possible scale spaces to a smaller class with few free parameters. The framework is very general, and different axiom sets yield different representations.

explainer.example: A team designing a multi-scale image analysis picks axioms such as smoothness and causality, then derives a representation family that satisfies them with a small number of tunable parameters.
